posts:
Winds of change buffet veterinary school accreditor as federal rules loom.
Evidence: Educational Freedom, Regulatory Dilution, Political Oversight
#HigherEd #Veterinary

The Education Department frames its accreditation overhaul as a victory for competition that dismantles monopoly gatekeeping by bodies like the AVMA COE to expand student access.
Stated Judgement: (+0.86, +0.94) — Greater Good

Ground reality reveals deregulation aimed at lowering clinical training bars for proprietary programs, inviting political interference while threatening veterinary standards.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.71, -0.75) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Destruction. Deregulatory pretexts dismantle established professional clinical safeguards.
Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 14.8, z: 3)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- U.S. Dept of Ed: FAIL (-0.75, -0.80) — Undermines standards under pretexts.
- AVMA COE Defense: COND (0.20, -0.10) — Defends quality but protects cartel power.
- LMU Litigation: FAIL (-0.65, -0.70) — Lawsuit sought lower accreditation bars.
The Department of Education has proposed rules overhauling higher education accreditation following the dismissal of an antitrust suit against the AVMA Council on Education.

The Bright Side:
Re-examining single-accreditor models can expose genuine administrative inertia, high compliance overhead, and bottlenecks that limit student enrollment in underserved rural veterinary disciplines.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The stated narrative confuses institutional competition (WHAT) with clinical training competence (WHO). While antitrust rhetoric attacks regulatory moats, veterinary medicine requires rigorous, hands-on hospital exposure that cannot be compromised for commercial expansion.

Social Physics Analysis:
The reform executes a Smart Selfish Maneuver where commercial universities and political appointees leverage free-market pretexts to dissolve professional accreditation autonomy. By manufacturing a narrative of unfair gatekeeping, policymakers project anti-consumer motives onto the accreditor while quietly extracting regulatory oversight. This lowers the capital threshold required to run clinical programs, shifting financial risk onto enrolled students and clinical risk onto the public.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. The erosion of peer accreditation destabilizes professional standards, ultimately yielding sub-standard clinical training pipelines.

The Unavoidable Truth: Lowering accreditation bars prioritizes institutional revenue over animal welfare.

The Unavoidable Lie: Federal political intervention is merely aimed at protecting consumer choice.

Alethekanon:
Dismantling specialized peer accreditation under the banner of deregulation replaces clinical domain competence with politicized administrative control. When standards yield to market pretexts, systemic quality collapses.

Awwthekanon:
Every pet owner knows how much trust goes into handing a sick family member over to a veterinarian. Diluting the education and clinical rigor of those who care for our most vulnerable companions just to cut costs breaks that sacred bond of care.

Brothekanon:
They claim they are busting monopolies so more folks can become vets, but really they just want diploma mills to churn out degrees without paying for actual animal hospitals. That is not cheaper school, that is bad medicine.

Spirithekanon:
"A false balance is an abomination to the Lord, but a just weight is His delight." Proverbs 11:1 FAIL
Gutting rigorous accreditation standards under the pretext of market competition sacrifices professional health standards for institutional profit.
